title: Rolling Window
body:
A **rolling window** recomputes a statistic over a sliding fixed-length period, producing a
series that shows how the statistic itself changed over time.

```
window = 60 trading days

day 60:   compute over days 1-60
day 61:   compute over days 2-61
day 62:   compute over days 3-62      ...
```

The reason is that a single number computed over ten years hides everything that happened
inside them. One volatility figure for 2015 through 2025 averages a calm decade with the March
2020 crash, and reports neither.

Plotted against time, rolling [[Volatility]] makes a crisis visible as a spike, and a rolling
[[Sharpe Ratio]] shows that risk-adjusted performance is a moving quantity and never a
fixed property of a strategy.

The window length is the trade-off:

```
short window    reacts quickly to a change, and is noisy
long window     smooth and stable, and lags the change it is reporting
```

Nothing is available for the first $n-1$ days, since the window has insufficient data, which is
why a rolling plot starts later than the price series it came from.
